text.p: Citibank launched on Tuesday a fully licensed bank in Romania, Citibank Romania SA to serve global coporations and local companies and help develop businesses in the ex-communist country.

William Rhodes, vice chairman of Citibank NA, said at a inauguration ceremony that the opening of the Bucharest-based subsidiary showed Citibank's confidence in Romania's ability to pursue economic reforms.
Citibank, which opened a representative office in Bucharest in 1995, played a major role in Romania's attempts to re-enter world capital markets two years ago after 15 years of absence.

Last year, Citibank also arranged syndicated loans for Romania's state air traffic control service Romtehnica R.A. to buy radar equipment and for the state-run bank Banca Romana de Comert Exterior Bancorex SA to fund farm equipment.

"Citibank will continue to help the country finance infrastructure projects and to support the National Bank of Romania in its external financing strategy," said David Garner, president of Citibank Romania.
Romania's National Bank announced plans to raise up to $1.6 billion from the international capital markets this year.
The acitivity of Citibank Romania would initially focus on cash management, treasury and money market operations.
"Citibank's long-term goal in Romania is to become a major local bank and an integral part of the banking system," Rhodes said.
Romania has about 40 banks, of which 14 are subsidiaries, branches or representative offices of foreign banks.
